third_addendum_written_before_the_run.why: The independent CLAIM reviewer REFUTED item 3's reasoning while agreeing with its direction, and its reading is sharper than mine. NEMO's barotropic correction is NOT an additive constant: stprk3_stg.F90:440 builds zub = uu_b(Kaa) - SUM(e3u_0*uu(:,Kaa))*r1_hu_0 from the SOLVE OUTPUT, so it is a rank-1 operator that turns a single-level error into a column-uniform image of itself. A level-30-only error d becomes (1-f)*d at level 30 and -f*d at levels 1..29 with f = e3t(30)/hu_0. The reviewer read f = 0.069921 off NEMO's own ladder parameters (usrdef_zgr.F90:133-137) and matched THREE observed statistics to four significant figures on that one constant. So the measured error is exactly ONE bad number per column, at the deepest wet level, and levels 1..29 are its barotropic image -- and my column-uniformity test, while it does rule out an error in zub itself, cannot separate the two level-30 candidates.

The quantity it actually predicts is the PRE-correction single-cell error, d = e(30)/(1-f) = 1.0195e-06. P4g's predicted 1.022324152002595e-06 sits 0.3 per cent from that, not 8 per cent.

REFUTE (slope outside 0.9..1.1 or R-squared below 0.9) => the peak agreement was a coincidence of the maxima and no owner is named.
